collections.special_event_steps.ayako_re: Just past nine in the morning, the hallways gradually quieted down after morning handover.

In the doctors' lounge, Ryuji Sakaguchi had just handed an interdepartmental follow-up record back to Shiori Fujisaki, setting two freshly poured cups of warm black tea onto the small round table while he was at it.
Shiori Fujisaki accepted her teacup and neatly closed the folder, a gentle, unhurried smile touching her lips:
"Thank you, Dr. Sakaguchi. With those postoperative observation points you just added, following up this afternoon will be so much smoother."
"Think nothing of it. It's rare to see your schedule with breathing room today—no morning outpatient clinic?"
"Mm, I deliberately kept this little window around nine open. A guest with an advance appointment is coming by the hospital today to complete some paperwork—"
Before she even finished speaking, the smartphone resting on the table buzzed softly twice.
Shiori Fujisaki glanced down to tap the screen awake, then looked back up, her eyes curving warmly:
"Speak of the devil—she says she's already entered the first-floor lobby and is heading up in the elevator."
Ryuji Sakaguchi picked up his teacup and asked casually:
Just then, Kaori Miyama—who was passing the doorway with an armful of ER observation charts—paused slightly, stopping beside the half-open door to chime in:
"A visitor heading this way at nine o'clock... Don't tell me some pharmaceutical rep wandered onto the wrong floor?"
Shiori Fujisaki turned toward Dr. Miyama and blinked, her tone as calm as if she were reading the weather forecast:
"Not a pharmaceutical rep. Both Dr. Miyama and Dr. Sakaguchi should still remember her—it's Ayako. Ayako Katagiri."
Visibly, the air inside the lounge froze for a full second.
The teacup in Ryuji Sakaguchi's hand stopped midair:
Kaori Miyama's relaxed shoulders stiffened on the spot. Almost by pure reflex, she flipped open today's schedule sheet in her hands, her brows snapping tightly together:
"Hold on. I don't have a single gastric surgery scheduled this morning or afternoon, and the ER hasn't admitted any patient named Ayako Katagiri—what is she doing at the hospital?"
Ryuji Sakaguchi set his teacup down, a complicated expression crossing his face:

"It's been over half a year since that incident... She actually dares set foot inside Hoshimi Hospital again? Don't tell me she ran into another 'super helpful person' downstairs and is getting changed right now for some new brand of immersive research."
Kaori Miyama's gaze sharpened, and she turned on her heel to head straight out the door:

"I'm calling the fourth-floor nurses' station on the internal line right now and telling Nanase to lock down the changing rooms and surgical corridor—under no circumstances can we let her get her hands on a patient wristband again."
Watching the two of them go on red alert as if bracing for an invasion, Shiori Fujisaki couldn't help lifting a hand to her lips with a soft laugh:

"Please calm down, you two. Ayako isn't here as an outpatient today, and she isn't sneaking in either—she submitted a formal application to the Director's Office through me a week ago, and she's coming in openly through proper channels today."
"A formal application? After we opened her up by mistake, it's already miraculous enough that she didn't blacklist Hoshimi Hospital for life—what is she applying to come back for?"
A bright, spirited woman's voice brimming with energy suddenly rang out from beside the half-open lounge doorframe.
All three of them turned to look at the same time.

Peeking around the doorframe was a head crowned with a signature high ponytail of silvery-violet hair. Twenty-five-year-old Ayako Katagiri had a bulging canvas art bag slung over her shoulder, her sparkling eyes curved into crescents as she waved enthusiastically at the three people inside:
"Good morning, Shiori! And Dr. Sakaguchi, Dr. Miyama—long time no see! I heard every word from out in the hall about locking up the fourth-floor changing rooms, you know!"

Kaori Miyama stared at the lively Ayako in the doorway, sizing her up from head to toe for two full seconds. Only after confirming she was wearing a normal pale-purple cardigan and trousers, with sneakers properly on her feet, did Dr. Miyama slowly let out a breath:
"...At least you're wearing your own clothes today."
Ayako Katagiri puffed out her chest and strolled grinning into the lounge:
"Well, obviously! Give me some credit—even I wouldn't trip over the exact same spot twice!"
"It's been half a year—seeing you so full of energy puts my mind at ease."
"Just to check first—you don't have any strange barcode wristbands on, right?"
Looking at Ayako beaming with vitality, Ryuji Sakaguchi couldn't help chuckling:
"It's been half a year—seeing you so full of energy puts my mind at ease. That incision on your abdomen has completely healed up by now, right?"
Ayako Katagiri patted her flat midriff, grinning from ear to ear:
"Completely healed! Even the scar has pretty much faded away—now I can pull an all-nighter drawing thirty pages of storyboards straight without even getting winded!"
Ryuji Sakaguchi let his gaze settle on her wrists and asked with deadpan seriousness:
"Welcome back, Ms. Katagiri. Just to be on the safe side, though, let me verify first—you aren't wearing any mysterious barcode wristbands today, are you?"
Ayako Katagiri burst out giggling and obligingly rolled up both sleeves, turning her wrists all the way around:
"Squeaky clean! Nothing here except a wristwatch and a hair tie—inspect away to your hearts' content, Doctors!"

Once the pleasantries were out of the way, Ayako Katagiri set her heavy canvas bag beside the round table, unzipped it with a loud zip, and—like someone showing off buried treasure—pulled out a finely printed sample issue of a shoujo manga magazine, sliding it in front of the three of them.

"Ta-daaa—! After I was discharged last time, I wove my operating-table perspective and recovery experience from those hospital days into a fictional hospital one-shot. It ran just last month, and guess what—it took second place in the reader survey for that issue!"
Mildly surprised, Ryuji Sakaguchi picked up the sample issue:
"Oh? Congratulations. Here I was worrying you'd turn 'Researching Manga Artist Suffers Botched Laparotomy' into an investigative expose series."
Ayako Katagiri waved her hands furiously:

"No way would I draw it like that! If I actually drew a patient mix-up, not only would the editorial legal team get a massive headache, it'd cause trouble for Shiori and all of you too, right? What I drew is a classic shoujo manga one-shot—the heroine is an ordinary girl rushed into the OR with an acute abdomen!"
Standing beside them, Kaori Miyama had just breathed a quiet sigh of relief when she leaned over for a casual glance at the page Sakaguchi had flipped open.
The very next second, Kaori Miyama's expression froze solid.

Right in the center of the double-page spread loomed a massive operating room surgical lamp. Beneath it stood a young dark-haired female surgeon in a surgical mask, her gaze as cold as frost, holding a gleaming scalpel steady in her fingers—while the speech bubble above her head reproduced a chilling line word for word:
"Panicking right now has zero medical value."
And in the panel right beside it stood a composed young male assistant, delivering a follow-up line to the heroine on the table in an utterly placid tone:
"Let's get you safely stitched back up first."
Ryuji Sakaguchi went silent for two seconds:
"...Why does that line look so awfully familiar?"
A vein at Kaori Miyama's temple gave a barely perceptible twitch. Pressing a slender finger down onto the magazine page, she lifted a cool gaze to Ayako:
Ayako Katagiri clapped her hands together in a plea, beaming brightly as she tried to smooth things over:

"Come on, call it touched-up details—artistic license! Besides, Dr. Miyama, you have no idea: the single most popular character in the fan mail was this 'deadpan ice-queen surgeon with the scalpel'! Several readers wrote in saying, 'A cool older-sister doctor who wouldn't bat an eye if the sky fell is just beyond cool—totally breathtaking!'"
Holding her teacup nearby, Shiori Fujisaki could barely contain her amusement:

"It startled me when I got my sample copy, too. Even without naming names, anyone who knows Dr. Miyama would probably recognize her within three seconds just from that look in her eyes while holding a scalpel."
Kaori Miyama shifted her gaze half an inch away and let out a quiet huff:
"...I was simply stating basic clinical common sense at the time. I had no intention of supplying you with flashy shoujo manga catchphrases."

With a sheepish giggle, Ayako Katagiri tucked the magazine away and promptly hauled out a hardcover sketchbook fully three fingers thick, its edge freshly lined with blank colored index tabs, slapping it down onto the table.

"Anyway, seeing how well the one-shot was received, my magazine editor asked if I wanted to strike while the iron's hot and expand it into a full-fledged long-form hospital serialization—preferably with some bizarre, over-the-top major surgery every single chapter!"
Ryuji Sakaguchi raised a brow at her:
"Sounds right up a commercial magazine's alley. Did you agree to draw it that way?"
Ayako Katagiri shook her head, tapping the sketchbook's cover lightly as the keen expression of a seasoned creator settled over her face:

"I went home, drafted two pages of an outline, and stopped right there. If you rely purely on gimmicky spectacle surgeries, readers get tired of it after two or three chapters once the novelty wears off. That can never carry a real long-running series—and it wouldn't be satisfying for me to draw, either."

She flipped the sketchbook open with a crisp rustle—nearly every page inside was still pristine white, save for the center of the flyleaf, where a tentative project title was written bold and proud in vivid purple marker:
Bracing both hands on the edge of the table, Ayako Katagiri looked around at the three of them with shining eyes:

"As for what the true centerpiece of a long-form series ought to be... honestly, I'm still figuring that out myself! After all, the last time I came to Hoshimi Hospital, I spent the first half groggy and knocked out on an operating table, and the second half obediently flat on my back nursing stitches—I didn't even make it halfway down the inpatient hallway."
She pointed to the rough few-stroke impression doodles sketched beneath the title on the flyleaf, her voice growing more excited by the second:

"Even so, just from the sounds I heard through my ward door during those few days and the way you all took turns coming in on rounds, my manga-artist intuition kept setting off sirens nonstop—this hospital is definitely hiding tons of treasure-trove material I never got the chance to see! So instead of locking myself in my studio making things up out of thin air, I applied to my editorial department for a one-month field research period and came running back to see everything from top to bottom!"
Kaori Miyama glanced down at the handful of stick-figure first-impression doodles tucked in the corner of the flyleaf, her brows furrowing again:
"...Hold on. Even if it's just an initial-impression memo, why does the little stick figure representing me have three shards of ice drawn floating over its head?"
Ayako Katagiri answered with unapologetic conviction:

"That's my first-impression icon left over from my hospital stay! Look at Dr. Sakaguchi's little figure right next to yours—I even tagged him with an unverified note saying 'Looks like a normal person, but surprisingly savage with dry remarks'! Who knows, after a month of observation it might even get an upgrade!"
"...Thanks for the glowing review, though that note really doesn't need any upgrading."
Smiling, Shiori Fujisaki glanced at her wristwatch and gently reminded her old classmate:

"All right, Ayako—keep flipping past the flyleaf and Dr. Miyama might confiscate your brand-new sketchbook on day one. It's almost time for our appointment with Director Asuka, so why don't we head to the Director's Office to take care of the formal paperwork first?"
Ayako Katagiri clapped a hand to her forehead:
"Ah, right, right! Today's number-one mission is picking up Director Shiromiya's official permit!"
Kaori Miyama set her stack of ER folders neatly onto the table and stood up crisply:
Expressionless, Kaori Miyama pulled open the door:

"Getting from here to the Director's Office means passing two stairwells and an elevator with direct access to the fourth-floor surgical wing. Until I watch you finish registering as an official visitor with my own eyes, I don't trust leaving you to roam the corridors unsupervised."
Ryuji Sakaguchi rose to his feet with a smile as well:
"In that case, I'll tag along and bear witness too."
Sunlight poured generously into the Director's Office.

Seated behind her wide desk, twenty-three-year-old Hospital Director Asuka Shiromiya held the "Long-Term Manga Research Residency Proposal" Ayako had sent ahead. After turning the final page with focused attention, she looked up at the four people standing neatly before her desk.

"Welcome back to Hoshimi Hospital, Ms. Katagiri. Seeing how tightly Dr. Miyama and Dr. Sakaguchi are escorting you today, I take it you didn't run into any unidentified 'helpful direction-givers' along the way?"
Sheepishly, Ayako Katagiri stuck out the tip of her tongue:
"Haha... I really caused you colossal trouble last time, Director Shiromiya! That's why I dutifully applied through proper channels a whole week in advance this time!"
The corners of Asuka Shiromiya's lips curved upward. Picking up the Director's seal from her desk, she stamped a crisp red impression onto the bottom of the application form:
"I've read through your proposal—it's fascinating. Effective today, I officially approve your thirty-day research residency here at Hoshimi Hospital."
Sliding the stamped permit across the desk, she held up three slender fingers and laid out the ground rules with brisk clarity and a touch of trademark Shiromiya dry humor:

"The rules are simple—just remember three things. First, you may only enter the public areas and designated clinical observation zones listed on your permit, and you must obtain consent before observing staff at work or interviewing them. Second, any material involving patients must be thoroughly anonymized, and you may not approach or disturb patients directly without dual permission from both the hospital and the patient. Third—and most important of all—you are strictly forbidden from touching any medical equipment, performing any medical procedures whatsoever, or letting anyone mistake you for actual medical staff."
Ayako Katagiri snapped her spine ramrod straight on the spot, raising her right hand beside her ear as solemnly as if taking an oath:

"I swear to obey every word! This time I will never, ever strip down into a patient gown again, and I will never, ever sneak barefoot into a fourth-floor operating room and climb onto an operating table!"
Beside her, Kaori Miyama added flatly:
"And don't slip any patient wristbands handed to you by strangers onto your wrist, either."
Ayako Katagiri nodded with fierce determination:
Her eyes curving in satisfaction, Asuka Shiromiya closed her folder, rose from her chair, and walked over to the wardrobe behind the side of her desk:

"Good spirit. Still, a hospital isn't a tourist attraction—if we let you wander the ward and clinic corridors every day in street clothes lugging that massive art bag, inpatients are bound to feel uneasy seeing a stranger staring around and sketching nonstop."
As she spoke, Asuka brought out a prepared long white gift box from the wardrobe, set it on the reception coffee table, and gently lifted the lid.

Neatly folded inside was a crisp, immaculately starched traditional white one-piece Hoshimi Hospital nurse uniform, topped squarely with a matching white nurse cap and a pair of soft-soled white nursing shoes.
Ayako Katagiri's eyes lit up in a flash:
"Waaah—!! Is this a Hoshimi Hospital nurse uniform?! Complete with the nurse cap too?!"
Asuka Shiromiya lifted the collar to show off the sleek, tailored lines along the waist, an unmistakable note of pride in her own uniform design sneaking into her voice:

"I had Dr. Fujisaki estimate the size based on your height. Wearing our hospital uniform will keep you from sticking out like a sore thumb when taking notes in the hallways—why not step into the adjoining changing room and see how it fits?"
Thrilled, Ayako Katagiri scooped the uniform box into her arms, wearing that exact same jackpot-winner grin from six months ago:
"Lucky—!! You understand me way too well, Director Shiromiya! I'll go change right away!!"
Watching her zip like a puff of smoke into the attached changing room, Ryuji Sakaguchi couldn't help murmuring to Asuka:
"Director Shiromiya... Didn't your third rule just say she's forbidden from letting anyone mistake her for actual medical staff? Is handing her a full nurse uniform and cap really wise?"
Asuka Shiromiya gave a mysterious wink, unhurriedly slipped one more item out of her desk drawer to tuck behind her back, and smiled without giving anything away:
"Rest assured, Dr. Sakaguchi. I've already prepared a foolproof safeguard against mistaken identity."
Five minutes later, the door to the adjoining changing room clicked open.

Ayako Katagiri stepped out dressed in the crisp, snow-white one-piece nurse uniform. Its fitted waist accented her trim, graceful figure to perfection, and the white nurse cap sat squarely atop her striking silvery-violet ponytail—leaving her looking both fresh and neat, yet practically fizzing with irrepressible energy.
Smoothing down her skirt hem, Ayako excitedly spun a half-turn on the spot in front of everyone:

"Well, well, how is it, Shiori? The size is spot-on! Who would've thought that besides lying on an operating table, I'd actually get to walk around a hospital fair and square in an authentic angel-in-white uniform!"
Shiori Fujisaki looked her old classmate up and down, genuine warmth rising in her eyes as she gently teased:

"It suits you wonderfully, Ayako—you look the part even better than I imagined. Though your eyes are sparkling like you're headed to an amusement park on a school trip, so you look way more curious than any real nurse here."
Smugly, Ayako Katagiri touched the brim of her nurse cap:
"Hehe, with an outfit buff like this, I feel like my storyboarding speed is gonna double—"
"Hold off on spinning around just yet, Ms. Katagiri. Stand still a moment—there's still one last, most essential standard accessory left to put on you."
Obediently, Ayako Katagiri puffed up her chest:
"Oh, is it a name badge like the one on Shiori's chest?"

From behind her back, Asuka Shiromiya produced a custom-made acrylic badge, lined it up right above Ayako's left breast pocket, clipped it firmly in place with a sharp click, and stepped half a pace back to admire her handiwork:
Inside the office, Sakaguchi, Miyama, and Fujisaki all turned their eyes to the left side of Ayako's chest at once.

Pinned squarely to the front of that immaculate, dignified nurse uniform was an extra-thick white-backed badge a full size larger all around than Hoshimi Hospital's standard staff ID. Not only were her name and title printed in crisp boldface, the enlarged warning across the bottom—deliberately framed in a bright red border—was so eye-poppingly prominent you could spot it from five meters away:

Ayako Katagiri
Manga Artist / Research Observer
[NO MEDICAL PROCEDURES PERMITTED]
Looking down and getting a clear view of the overwhelmingly conspicuous plaque on her chest, Ayako Katagiri froze for two seconds before her voice shot up half an octave:
"W-Wait a second, Director Shiromiya!! Isn't this badge a whole size bigger than Shiori's and all the nurses' badges out there?!"
Asuka Shiromiya tilted her head, appraising the proportions with dead-serious focus:

"Big? I think the visual balance against the uniform lapel is just right. Besides, considering how thick that incident report from six months ago was, if anything I still feel the red lettering at the bottom isn't big enough—just yesterday I was debating whether to custom-order you a reflective diagonal sash instead."
Clutching her chest, Ayako Katagiri looked ready to weep without tears:

"A reflective sash would make me look like someone handing out flyers in front of a department store!! With this giant plaque pinned on me, everyone's eyes get sucked straight to the red 'NO MEDICAL PROCEDURES PERMITTED' warning—it totally ruins the vibe of this gorgeous nurse uniform!"
Kaori Miyama, who had been watching with folded arms the entire time, wore a look of deep satisfaction for the first time all morning and gave a crisp nod:

"I wholeheartedly endorse the Director's sizing choice. Better yet, pin a matching one on her back too—that way, no matter which floor she wanders onto, not a single patient will ask her to swap an IV bottle, and no nurse will ever wheel her into an OR for surgical prep again."
Studying the oversized badge, Ryuji Sakaguchi added without batting an eye:

"Look on the bright side, Ms. Katagiri. Last time your issued outfit at Hoshimi Hospital was 'a patient gown with nothing underneath.' This time you get clothes, shoes, and you don't even have to lose a second appendix while we're at it—your benefits package just jumped three whole tiers."
The corner of Ayako Katagiri's eye twitched:
"Dr. Sakaguchi, you totally just cracked a pitch-black joke at my appendix's expense, didn't you?!"
Unable to hold back any longer, Shiori Fujisaki let out a soft laugh and stepped over to straighten her old friend's slightly crooked nurse cap:

"Come on now, it's actually pretty cute, Ayako. And I guarantee that with this oversized 'get-out-of-trouble-free plaque' on your chest, even if you zone out with your sketchbook in a corner of the hall, Head Nurse Ishigami probably won't draft you straight onto the night shift as she walks by."

Hearing that it would not only let her sketch freely, but also spare her from getting conscripted by a terrifying head nurse, Ayako Katagiri agonized for less than three seconds before her innate optimism won out completely.

Looking down, she flicked the oversized acrylic badge on her chest with a finger, pulled her sketchbook and pencil back out of her art bag, flipped open a fresh blank first page with a snap, and raised her head brimming with energy:

"...Fine then! Oversized it is—maxed-out recognizability counts as main-character treatment anyway! Well then, Director Shiromiya, Dr. Sakaguchi, Dr. Miyama, and Shiori—for thirty full days starting today, 'Tales of Hoshimi Hospital' Research Observer Ayako Katagiri is officially in your care!"

Watching the manga artist before them—topped with a nurse cap, sporting a giant '[NO MEDICAL PROCEDURES PERMITTED]' badge, and practically glowing with eagerness to scour every corner of the hospital for material—Kaori Miyama lightly pinched the bridge of her nose, while Ryuji Sakaguchi already had a sinking premonition that Hoshimi Hospital's corridors wouldn't know a single quiet day for the next month.
At one-thirty in the afternoon, midday ward rounds had just wrapped up.

Walking up to the third-floor nurses' station with two patient charts whose IV drip-rate orders he had just adjusted, Ryuji Sakaguchi spotted a striking flash of silvery-violet hair bobbing beneath a white nurse cap from down the hall.

Ayako Katagiri stood ramrod straight before the station counter, clutching her sticky-note-studded thick sketchbook tight to her chest as she faced Ren Nanase and Miyuki Asakura like a brand-new recruit reporting for duty.
Sharp-eyed Miyuki Asakura spotted Sakaguchi first, her lips immediately curving into a sweet, faintly teasing smile:

"Oh my, impeccable timing, Dr. Sakaguchi. Nanase and I are taking Ms. Katagiri along for inpatient ward nursing observation this afternoon—come to think of it, it really makes one sentimental. The last time the four of us were gathered together, Ms. Katagiri was lying stark naked on an operating table, and today she's finally standing beside one fully dressed."
Ayako Katagiri's cheeks flared crimson in an instant, and she covered the oversized badge on her chest in quiet protest:
"Ms. Asakura!! I swore I was turning the page on that chapter for good—how could you bring up my operating-table and surgical-prep dark history the second we meet?!"
Beside her, Ren Nanase wore a gentle, earnest expression as she reached over to double-check the badge clip above Ayako's left breast pocket:

"Your badge is pinned nice and secure, and the laces on your soft-soled shoes aren't loose either. Ms. Katagiri, while shadowing us this afternoon, just stay half a step diagonally behind Ms. Asakura and me. If a patient or family member happens to call out to you, don't panic—simply point to your badge, take half a step back, and leave the rest to us."
Ayako Katagiri nodded vigorously, flipped open a fresh page of her sketchbook with a crisp rustle, and gestured with boundless enthusiasm:

"Got it! Actually, from watching at a distance in the hallways over the past few days, I've already mapped out several classic highlight panels for nurses—like gently holding a patient's hand beside a sun-drenched window, dabbing sweat off a lead surgeon's forehead during an operation, or sprinting down the corridor pushing a gurney while shouting 'Coming through, critical patient!'"
Sliding the signed order sheets into the rack, Ryuji Sakaguchi raised a brow at what he was hearing:
"...That forehead-wiping panel—do you use that trope a lot in shoujo manga?"
Miyuki Asakura tilted her head and picked up the thread with a beaming smile:

"In a real operating room, if a scrub nurse dared touch the lead surgeon's forehead with sterile gloves, she'd probably get chased right back out to re-scrub the very next second. And as for sprinting down the hallway pushing a gurney and shouting—if Head Nurse Ishigami ever caught sight of that, our shift schedule for the entire month would become quite the spectacle."
"Huh?! You mean no wiping sweat AND no running?!"
Fighting back a smile, Ren Nanase picked up her rounds tray and temperature chart clipboard:
"Shall we head out, Ms. Katagiri? The two o'clock ward rounds are just about to start—walk one circuit with us and you'll see what an ordinary day actually looks like."

A little over an hour later, as Ryuji Sakaguchi stepped out of a room after double-checking dressing changes on several post-op patients in the third-floor east wing, he ran right into Ayako Katagiri around the corner of the corridor.

Compared to how radiant she had looked setting off, however, the twenty-five-year-old manga artist was now leaning against the hallway handrail catching her breath, her mechanical pencil flying across her sketchbook in frantic shorthand while even the white nurse cap atop her head had slipped half an inch askew.
Ryuji Sakaguchi slowed to a stop:
"What's with that face? Worn out after shadowing them for barely an hour?"
Ayako Katagiri looked up at the sight of Sakaguchi, her eyes wide with shell-shocked awe as she lowered her voice into a rapid-fire whisper:
"Dr. Sakaguchi!! Do all the nurses in your hospital have silent caster wheels built into the soles of their feet and automated scanners installed in their eyes?!"
Pointing a few paces ahead to where Ren Nanase and Miyuki Asakura stood on either side of a treatment cart cross-checking IV bags, she ticked items off on her fingers:

"In this one single hour, neither of them has taken so much as a sip of water! They cross-checked twelve identical-looking clear IV bags, casually adjusted drip rates for eight patients, swapped out drainage bags for three beds, answered four internal calls, and even helped an elderly lady fish her reading glasses out of the crack beside her mattress in between—meanwhile, my calves are already aching just from chasing after them trying to sketch!"

Right as she spoke, the forcedly cheerful voice of a young female post-op patient drifted through the half-open door of a nearby double room—"I'm fine, really, it doesn't hurt a bit! No need to bother calling a doctor—I can get out of bed and walk to the restroom all by myself right now!"
Ayako Katagiri had barely jotted down half a note reading "spirited patient in recovery" when Ren Nanase paused lightly outside the doorway.
Without bluntly calling the patient's bluff, Ren Nanase stepped gently just inside the threshold with her tray, her voice soft yet certain:

"Don't throw off your covers just yet. Your knuckles are white from gripping the bedrail, and there's cold sweat on your temples—did turning over tug on the right side of your abdominal binder? There's nothing embarrassing at all about hurting right after surgery. Let me lower the head of your bed five degrees and readjust your binder tension first, okay?"

Silence fell inside the room for two seconds before the young woman who had been putting on such a brave front softened all at once: "...Mm. Truth is, my right side has been throbbing and pulling nonstop just now... Sorry for the trouble, Nurse Nanase."
Out in the corridor, Ayako Katagiri stared slack-jawed:
"Whoa... Even through a mostly closed door while the patient was smiling, how on earth did Ms. Nanase see right through her tough act at a single glance?!"
Hardly had the words left her mouth when Miyuki Asakura's impeccably sweet voice floated out from the doorway of a room across the hall:
"Oh my, Miss in Bed Five—surely you haven't twisted the cap off that bottle of iced fizzy juice tucked under your pillow yet, have you?"

A flustered rustling sounded inside the ward. Wearing a smile as gentle as a spring breeze, Miyuki Asakura held out her slender hand and, within three seconds flat, disarmed the patient into meekly surrendering the contraband cold drink without firing a shot:

"If you drink carbonated iced juice before your bowels have officially started moving again, your tummy will puff up like a balloon later—and then we'd have to put a nasogastric tube back in for decompression, you know. Let me keep this safe for you in the nurses' station fridge for now, and once Dr. Sakaguchi clears you for a liquid diet, I'll bring it right back, all right?"
Watching Miyuki Asakura stroll smiling back to the treatment cart with her confiscated spoils in hand, Ayako Katagiri instinctively shrank her neck in and scribbled furiously across her sketchbook:

"...They're terrifyingly good. One is so gentle it's like she has a mind-reading radar built in, and the other makes people lay down their arms with one smiling sentence... Now I completely understand how this hospital manages to stay running!"
"Surgeons only cover the hour or two on the table; they watch over everything else."
"So never let their gentle smiles fool you—nothing gets past their eyes."
Watching the two nurses sort supplies in seamless sync beside the treatment cart, Ryuji Sakaguchi spoke in a calm, grounded voice:

"Surgeons only handle the hour or two on the operating table. Whether a patient walks out of here safe and sound afterward depends on them keeping watch in the wards for the remaining twenty-two hours of the day."
Tightening her grip on her pencil, Ayako Katagiri gave a thoughtful, emphatic nod:
"Twenty-two hours... No wonder even just watching them from the hallway, you can feel such steady, reassuring strength in everything they do!"
Ryuji Sakaguchi let out a quiet chuckle:
"So never let their gentle demeanor fool you. Whether someone's sneaking drinks or gritting their teeth through pain, practically nothing in the inpatient ward gets past their eyes."
Feeling that down to her bones, Ayako Katagiri patted her chest:

"Thank goodness I've got my official get-out-of-trouble-free plaque on today—otherwise I get the feeling Ms. Nanase would even see right through the instant noodles I stayed up eating late last night!"
At three-thirty in the afternoon, having wrapped up a full circuit of rounds and handover log checks, Ren Nanase and Miyuki Asakura returned to the nurses' station to tidy their treatment trays.

Standing tucked against the outer corner of the station, Ayako Katagiri flipped back to the first page of her sketchbook. Looking at the panel she had drawn before noon—an "angel in white by a window showered in drifting rose petals"—she couldn't help snorting with laughter at herself. In the blank margin beside it, she sketched a pair of sturdy, nimble soft-soled white nursing shoes, followed by a uniform pocket crammed full of three-color ballpoint pens, medical tape, hemostats, and a pocket watch.
"Rose petals, my foot... Jam-packed pockets and a stopwatch are way cooler than that anyway..."
Just as she set her canvas art bag down by her feet and rose onto her tiptoes to sketch one more panel of the shift whiteboard inside the station—
Without warning, both the temperature and the low murmur of conversation along the inpatient corridor dropped sharply in unison.
The steady, measured click of heels—without a trace of wasted weight or variation in tempo—approached from down the hall.
Carrying a hospital-wide nursing inspection binder under one arm, Director of Nursing Chizuru Ishigami walked quietly over from the elevator lobby.
At virtually the exact same split second, Ren Nanase and Miyuki Asakura paused their small talk and straightened up naturally in poised greeting:
"Good afternoon, Head Nurse. All afternoon IV replacements and postoperative rounds on the third floor have been completed on schedule."

Chizuru Ishigami gave a slight nod, sparing not a single syllable of empty pleasantry. Her cool, striking gaze swept smoothly across the station counter before coming to an unhurried rest on nurse-capped Ayako Katagiri in the corner—or to be exact, pausing for a full second on the oversized '[NO MEDICAL PROCEDURES PERMITTED]' red-lettered badge pinned to her left chest.

The woman hadn't frowned or raised her voice in the slightest, yet every hair on the back of Ayako Katagiri's neck stood straight on end. As if someone had slammed a pause button on her, she snapped her heels together at rigid attention, pressing her sketchbook flat against the side of her skirt:

"G-Good afternoon, Head Nurse Ishigami!! I'm Manga Research Observer Ayako Katagiri!! I've stayed half a step back all afternoon like clockwork and haven't laid a finger on a single cart or IV bottle!!"
Suppressing a smile nearby, Ryuji Sakaguchi put in a word for her:
"She really has followed the rules to the letter all afternoon—just trailing behind Nanase and Asakura taking notes."
Having heard them out, Chizuru Ishigami showed no change in expression, her voice as cool and level as if auditing inventory figures:
Her gaze shifted half an inch downward, settling on the canvas art bag by Ayako's feet where it jutted slightly past the yellow clearance line at the corner:
"Tuck your bag ten centimeters further in. Crash carts and dressing carts turn tight around this corner—leave nothing underfoot that could trip someone."
Moving faster than she ever had in her life, Ayako bent down, scooped the art bag tight into her arms, and barely dared to breathe.
Satisfied that the passageway was completely clear, Chizuru Ishigami inclined her head briefly to Ryuji Sakaguchi and glanced over the log sheet in Ren Nanase's hand:
"Keep a close eye on the color of Bed Four's drainage fluid tonight; page the on-call surgeon immediately if anything changes. Carry on."
With that, she turned and walked unhurriedly down the corridor.

Not until that cool, poised figure vanished completely into the stairwell did Ayako Katagiri let out a massive "Phew—!" like a diver breaking the surface from the deep sea, her knees nearly buckling against the edge of the counter:
"Th-That scared the life out of me...! She didn't even scold me, so why did one look at my badge dredge up the exact same guilty panic as getting caught doodling manga in class back in third grade?!"
Miyuki Asakura covered her lips with a soft laugh:
"Passing inspection with nothing worse from Head Nurse Ishigami than 'tuck your bag ten centimeters further in' already makes you a full-marks rookie, Ms. Katagiri."
From behind the counter, Ren Nanase poured a small paper cup of warm barley tea and handed it to Ayako with a gentle smile:
"Thank you for keeping up with us all afternoon—your feet must be aching, right? Have a sip of tea and rest a bit."

Accepting the warm paper cup, Ayako Katagiri glanced down at her densely filled sketchbook, then back up at the bustling yet immaculately orderly nurses' station, excitement sparking bright in her eyes once again:
"Worth every single ache! Just the details I gathered this afternoon beat ten reference books cooked up at home—thank you so much, Ms. Nanase, Ms. Asakura, and Dr. Sakaguchi!"
Everyone in Your Hospital Is Weird
Five-ten in the evening, marking two full weeks of the research residency.

When Ryuji Sakaguchi and Kaori Miyama—fresh off her daytime ER shift—pushed open the doctors' lounge door one after the other, they found Shiori Fujisaki already standing beside the large round table. And the entire tabletop, ordinarily reserved for tea sets and medical journals, was completely blanketed with over a dozen densely drawn B4 manga character concept sheets.
Dressed in her white nurse uniform and cap, Ayako Katagiri stood hands on hips beside the table. Spotting Sakaguchi and Miyama walk in, she immediately waved them over, positively beaming:

"Aha! Dr. Sakaguchi, Dr. Miyama—perfect off-shift timing! Come look, come look—after two solid weeks of dedicated observation at Hoshimi Hospital, the first batch of main character prototype sheets for 'Tales of Hoshimi Hospital' is finally done!"
Kaori Miyama halted in her tracks, narrowing her eyes warily at the sea of white paper:
"...Fair warning: if anything on that table violates the Director's anonymization rules, I'm confiscating it on behalf of the Director's Office right now."
Patting the oversized acrylic badge on her chest, Ayako Katagiri swore up and down:

"How could I possibly break the rules! I'm a pro shoujo manga artist, you know! Every single character's name, visual detail, and backstory has gone through my airtight artistic remixing and camouflage—I guarantee no outsider could ever guess who they're based on, and you guys might not even recognize yourselves!"
Standing beside the table with a cup of hot tea in hand, Shiori Fujisaki offered an extraordinarily delicate, hesitant smile:
"Well... Ayako, when it comes to the 'not even recognizing ourselves' part, I think you might be just a tiny bit overconfident."
Ryuji Sakaguchi stepped up and casually picked up the outermost management concept sheet.

The left half depicted a baby-faced young female hospital director with a side ponytail, eyes gleaming as she circled a green sterile surgical gown with a tailor's measuring tape, a speech bubble beside her proclaiming: 'Who ever decreed a sterile surgical gown can't have a flattering waistline?'; the right half showed a tall, glacial nursing commander in a dark uniform whose mere passage turned every background speech bubble down the corridor into '......... (Muted)', while a trembling little critter in the corner frantically tucked an art bag ten centimeters closer to the baseboard.
Ryuji Sakaguchi was silent for a second:
"...Director Shiromiya and Head Nurse Ishigami. Would anyone on earth need more than two seconds to figure that out?"
Ayako Katagiri pointed indignantly at the sheet:
"I switched which side Director Shiromiya wears her hair ornament on, and I even changed her name to 'Asuna Shirokiya', okay?!"
Deadpan, Kaori Miyama plucked up the second department-ensemble sketch and gave it a quick scan:

"And what about this 'blue-haired department chief wielding a mysterious pixelated metal rod down the second-floor hall while eagerly inviting young nurses to serve as live teaching aids'—plus 'the pharmacist big sister next to her locking the dispensary window at 5:01 p.m. on the dot to go buy limited-edition Mont Blancs'? All original artistic inventions of yours too?"
Ayako Katagiri stuck out her tongue:

"Watching Chief Mizuki call out 'Come be my ten-minute demo model, pretty please!' in the hallway packed way too much visual punch—leaving that out would be a crime against the manga world! Same goes for Ms. Iimura in Pharmacy, Dr. Nanjo who reads minds at a glance, dependable older-sister Dr. Jinguji, and the twin pillars of gentleness Ms. Sugimura and Ms. Nanase—honestly, grab any random person in your hospital and they've got enough character traits to carry an entire collected volume in another series!"
Ryuji Sakaguchi's eyes skimmed over an adjacent sheet shaded in gray screentone:
"You even drew the 'ice-beauty radiologist' holed up reading scans in the darkroom?"

"Sure, Dr. Misono barely says a word normally and gives off this chilly low-pressure aura up close, but the moment she sits down before a lightbox pointing out shadows and delivering her read, her side profile looks straight out of a movie still!"
Kaori Miyama lifted half a draft tucked underneath, the corner of her mouth twitching:

"Plus this female surgeon 'whose memory at the operating table rivals a supercomputer, yet asks her assistant what their name was again three seconds after stepping off'... If Dr. Haruka ever saw this sheet, she'd probably forget who drew it the moment she turned around."
Right next to those, Ryuji Sakaguchi spotted the three lead-perspective character sheets laid out dead center on the round table.

The first depicted an elegant headband-wearing, textbook-perfect all-rounder female doctor whose every gesture radiated poised grace amid a dazzling shoujo backdrop of drifting rose petals and starry screentone—save for a tiny gap-moe chibi tucked into the lower-left corner: that very same untouchable Madonna standing before a hospital dessert vending machine, agonizing in dead-serious silence for five straight minutes between the 'Caramel Pudding' and 'Strawberry Panna Cotta' buttons.
A faint blush rose across Shiori Fujisaki's fair cheeks, and she tapped her old friend's forehead in helpless exasperation:
"Ayako... I only mentioned that vending-machine story in passing over afternoon tea last week. Why would you put a tiny thing like that onto an official character sheet?"
Rubbing her forehead, Ayako Katagiri giggled:
"Because a hundred-out-of-a-hundred honor student getting stumped over pudding is the kind of contrast readers go crazy for!"

Ryuji Sakaguchi shifted his gaze to his own sheet in the middle—surrounded by medical staff sporting built-in lightning bolts, ice shards, roses, and holy halos, the male surgeon alone was rendered in clean, grounded lines, accompanied by a bold red margin note: 'The sole normal-looking straight man anchored at the eye of the hospital's eccentric hurricane (surprisingly rock-steady once he picks up a scalpel).'
Ryuji Sakaguchi arched a brow at Ayako:
"How come everyone else gets background special effects while I look like an ordinary office worker who wandered onto a fantasy film set?"
Ayako Katagiri held up an index finger with utter solemnity:

"You don't understand, Dr. Sakaguchi! In the middle of an explosively eccentric cast, you HAVE to have an emotionally stable normal person acting as the anchor—otherwise the whole manga will launch right out of the stratosphere!"
Before she even finished, Kaori Miyama—holding the last character sheet beside him—let out a faint crack of her knuckles.

Sakaguchi glanced sideways—only to see a sheet labeled 'Kaori Mitsuki, the Deadpan Truth-Seeking ER Doctor.' Not only did three crystal-clear ice shards float neatly above her head, the lower-right corner even featured a bonus four-panel gag strip: the stoic doctor cleaving open a treasure chest sealed with an 'Acute Abdomen?' talisman, finding it completely empty inside, and—far from looking disappointed—clasping her hands amid a beatific, saintly glow: 'Thank goodness, there's nothing inside at all!'
Kaori Miyama drew a deep breath, a vein pulsing faintly at her temple as she spoke one measured word at a time:

"Ayako Katagiri. Leave everyone else's sheets however you please, but you are erasing this 'cleaving open an empty treasure chest' four-panel strip in the bottom right this instant. Since when have I ever treated a patient's abdominal cavity like a treasure hunt?!"
In a single bound, Ayako Katagiri ducked behind Shiori Fujisaki, poking half her head out in self-defense:
"It's symbolism—pure symbolism! It shows your noble healer's heart, Dr. Miyama, genuinely rejoicing in a patient's health even when you come up empty-handed!!"

Just as Kaori Miyama reached out to snatch the eraser from Ayako's hand, Ryuji Sakaguchi's eyes fell upon the largest, most extravagantly rendered double-page two-person spread at the very top of the round table.
Flanking the left and right sides of the spread stood two formidable female surgeons locked in razor-sharp tension—
Studying the double-page spread, Ryuji Sakaguchi remarked offhandedly:
"Now this one genuinely nails the intensity of a hot-blooded shonen arch-rival showdown... Though if the two subjects ever saw it in person—"
Standing nearest the doorway, Shiori Fujisaki happened to glance out into the corridor. Her expression shifted ever so slightly, and she murmured:
"Ah... Ayako, I'm afraid it's a little too late to put this page away."
The sliding door of the lounge glided crisply open.

Having just wrapped up her afternoon inspection of major surgeries, Chief Surgeon Emiko Mido strode inside and headed straight toward the espresso machine in the corner; barely two seconds behind her, Deputy Chief of Surgery Artoria Pendragon stepped through the doorway with ramrod-straight posture, tomorrow's OR schedule clipped under her arm:
"Dr. Mido, regarding tomorrow morning's senior scrub nurse assignments for Operating Rooms One and Two, there is one remaining detail I need to verify with you—"
Emiko Mido slowed her pace slightly and turned halfway around:

Seeing both models come to a halt less than two paces from the big round table, Ayako Katagiri nearly jumped out of her skin. Letting out a tiny "Yipe!", she lunged forward with arms flung wide to shield the double-page showdown spread on the tabletop—

Only for the oversized acrylic badge on her chest to clack against the edge of the paper in the scramble, sending the lightning-drenched twin-titan standoff spread skidding straight across the slick tabletop to land right beneath the noses of Emiko Mido and Artoria!
Dead silence descended upon the lounge in an instant.

Ayako Katagiri froze over the edge of the table, both hands still outstretched in a desperate 'wait, come back!' reach; Kaori Miyama wordlessly took half a step back to disavow all involvement; Shiori Fujisaki lifted a slender hand to cover the corners of her mouth.
Holding her cup of black coffee, Emiko Mido cast a cool, downward glance over the sheet on the table.
Taking in the aloof 'Lone-Wolf Queen of the Scalpel' on the left side of the spread, Emiko Mido didn't show a trace of anger—instead, she calmly took a sip of black coffee and spoke in an even tone:
"The anatomical proportions and the wrist mechanics on the scalpel grip aren't half bad for an amateur. However, Ms. Katagiri."
Sweating bullets, Ayako Katagiri snapped to attention on the spot:
"Y-Yes, ma'am!! Go right ahead, Chief Mido!!"
Emiko Mido slid a sidelong, half-amused glance toward Artoria beside her:
"Framing Dr. Pendragon and me as an even fifty-fifty standoff—aren't you harboring a rather charitable misconception about the actual hierarchy of surgical skill in this department?"
Beside her, Artoria—who had been studying the drawing intently—gave an almost imperceptible twitch of her golden cowlick.

Though standing only 154 centimeters tall, the formidable Deputy Chief of Surgery closed her eyes for half a beat, then opened those clear, piercing emerald eyes—her spine straighter than a ruler and her tone impeccably prim and earnest:

"Dr. Mido, I cannot pretend I didn't hear that remark. Whether in lead-surgeon success rates on complex cases last quarter or departmental perioperative management scores, I do not recall trailing behind you in a single metric. Furthermore, Ms. Katagiri—"
Artoria turned her head and pointed with utter seriousness toward the bottom-right corner of the page:

"While I have every respect for a creator's artistic license, there are two objective factual inaccuracies I must ask you to correct. First, this is a modern surgical hospital; I would never rest my hand upon a sword hilt when discussing clinical matters with colleagues in the corridor. Second, when I meet Dr. Mido eye to eye, I do so through upright posture and professional conviction—not by standing atop a wooden booster crate."
Desperately stifling a laugh before she burst, a beet-red Ayako Katagiri bowed again and again:
"I-I'm so sorry!! I only sketched in that translucent little wooden crate offhand for compositional balance—I'll white it out the second I get back tonight!!"
A cool smirk tugged at the corner of Emiko Mido's lips:
"Oh? So there wasn't a wooden crate after all? At first glance just now, I was rather impressed by Ms. Katagiri's eye for realism."
Dignified fighting spirit flared instantly in Artoria's emerald eyes:

"Dr. Mido. Between tomorrow's OR assignments and this supposed 'hierarchy of skill' you just mentioned, it appears we ought to step into the conference room next door, lay out this month's statistical tables, and audit them line by line."
Emiko Mido lifted her coffee cup and turned on her heel:
As the two of them strode out the lounge doorway one behind the other, the air between them practically seemed to throw off a shower of invisible, frost-sharp sparks.
"...In a sense, that background lightning you drew really is 100% true to life."
"Better pack those sketches up fast before the next subject walks through the door."
Looking from the empty doorway back down to the lightning-filled spread on the table, Ryuji Sakaguchi remarked with heartfelt admiration:
"...In a sense, that background lightning you drew really is a hundred percent true to life—not an ounce of artistic exaggeration in sight."
Catching the faint sound of footsteps out in the corridor, Ryuji Sakaguchi prompted the still-rooted Ayako:

"Shouldn't you pack up this table full of character sheets before you trigger a full-blown diplomatic incident? Leave them spread out five minutes longer, and if Chief Mizuki happens to push that door open next, you can kiss clocking out tonight goodbye."

To everyone's surprise, far from being scared off by the near-death encounter just now, Ayako Katagiri cupped both cheeks in her hands, her eyes blazing like twin miniature suns as she gave an excited little hop right on the spot:

"Lucky—!! Did you see that just now?! That sidelong look Chief Mido gave over her black coffee, and the exact angle Deputy Chief Artoria's cowlick bobbed while she deadpan-refuted the booster crate—real life is ten times more amazing than anything I could make up on my own!!"
Snatching up her pencil, she leaned over the table to dash off a few quick strokes on the back of the draft, then beamed radiantly up at the exasperated trio of Sakaguchi, Miyama, and Fujisaki:
"Everyone in this hospital from top to bottom is completely weird, sure—but I think I'm finally starting to see what this manga is truly meant to be about!"
Kaori Miyama rubbed her temples and turned to Ryuji Sakaguchi:
"...Two whole weeks left. Sakaguchi, I'm already starting to miss the days when she stayed quietly in bed and only sketched photos of her own surgical field."
Shiori Fujisaki covered her lips with a gentle laugh:
"Look on the bright side, Dr. Miyama—at least Ayako promised to erase your 'empty treasure chest' gag strip."
Stuffing her sheets swiftly back into her portfolio, Ayako Katagiri muttered guiltily under her breath:
"...Honestly, I still think that treasure-chest metaphor was super spot-on—saving it as a bonus four-panel in the collected volume wouldn't hurt, right...?"
"Waaah—I'm erasing it, I swear I'll rub every trace clean tonight!!"
Was Shiori Like This Back Then Too?

At five-twenty in the evening, the bustle of the outpatient wing had gradually ebbed away, and slanting rays of sunset filtered through the glass-walled courtyard gallery to cast pools of warm amber across the pale wood-grain tables.

Carrying two next-day preoperative recheck summary sheets fresh from the clinical lab, Ryuji Sakaguchi rounded the corner of the courtyard and spotted Shiori Fujisaki and Ayako Katagiri sharing a pot of Darjeeling tea on a window-side bench.
For once, the sketchbook in front of Ayako lay closed; the two old friends had their heads together over an old photo on a phone screen, sharing light, familiar laughter.
Shiori Fujisaki looked up first as Sakaguchi approached, her eyes curving into an effortless smile:
"Dr. Sakaguchi—just heading back from the lab?"
Stepping over to the table, Ryuji Sakaguchi handed one of the recheck sheets to her:

"Yeah, I picked up the coagulation and electrolyte recheck sheet for your patient tomorrow morning while I was there. Every single value looks normal—I can sign off on the tail end of the joint consult when I head back to the office in a bit, so you don't have to make another trip up to the third floor."
Back when they first started working together, Shiori Fujisaki would never clock out without personally double-checking every piece of paperwork for her patients down to the final punctuation mark.

Right now, however, she scanned the key figures on the sheet, confirmed everything was in order, and let the tension she had carried all afternoon melt from her shoulders, a faintly weary yet remarkably soft smile gracing her lips:

"You're a lifesaver... After seeing over a dozen follow-up patients back-to-back this afternoon, my eyes really are starting to ache. In that case, I'll slack off a little today and leave that last half-page of the consult note in your hands, Dr. Sakaguchi?"
"Leave it to me. Enjoy your tea while it's warm and take your time catching up."

The moment he finished speaking, Ayako Katagiri—seated across the table—propped her cheeks in both hands and stared unblinkingly at Shiori Fujisaki with amethyst eyes, as though she had just stumbled upon a priceless rarity.
Caught off guard by her old classmate's stare, Shiori Fujisaki self-consciously touched a hand to her cheek:
"...What is it, Ayako? Do I have a tea stain on my face?"
Ayako Katagiri shook her head, her lips slowly curving into a teasing, nostalgic grin:
"No tea stain. It just hit me how surreal that was—did the words 'slack off a little' seriously just roll smooth as silk off our Miss Fujisaki's tongue?"
The tips of Shiori Fujisaki's ears warmed almost imperceptibly, and she raised her teacup for a light sip to hide it:
"It's the end of the workday—leaning on a dependable colleague once in a while is perfectly normal."
Turning toward Ryuji Sakaguchi before he could leave, Ayako Katagiri patted the empty seat beside her and waved him over eagerly:
"Take a five-minute breather with us, Dr. Sakaguchi! Let me tell you—back in our school days, you wouldn't believe what a terrifying iron-woman honor student Shiori used to be!"
Taking a seat beside the table, Ryuji Sakaguchi looked with keen interest toward the mildly exasperated Fujisaki:
"Oh? Very different from how she is now?"
Setting her teacup down, Shiori Fujisaki shot her old friend a gentle, chiding look:
"Ayako, that's ancient history from ages ago—no embellishing embarrassing stories about me in front of a colleague."
Grinning, Ayako Katagiri held up a finger:

"Nothing's embellished—every word is gospel truth! Did you know, Dr. Sakaguchi, in our second year of high school I fell a whole week behind in World History and Classical Literature rushing an exhibition piece for the art club, so right before finals I went crying to Shiori to borrow her class notes as a lifeline."
Framing a neat rectangle over the tabletop with both hands, she spoke with theatrical flair yet unmistakable admiration:

"And those three notebooks Shiori lent me? Not only was the handwriting neat enough to send straight to a printing press, every key point was strictly color-coded across three tiers in red, blue, and green—and wildest of all, not a single page corner had even half a millimeter of a dog-ear! I didn't even dare use an eraser near them while copying, terrified that dropping one crumb of eraser dust would be desecrating a work of art!"
Glancing at the stack of follow-up folders beside Fujisaki's hand—forever aligned to razor perfection—Ryuji Sakaguchi nodded in complete understanding:
"That part is completely believable. Her patient charts are still the neatest in the entire hospital."
A touch bashful, Shiori Fujisaki traced the handle of her teacup with a fingertip:
"Keeping things organized up front was just a habit back then... Besides, didn't you pass those finals smoothly in the end, Ayako?"
Ayako Katagiri chuckled, resting her chin in her palm and tilting her head as she watched her old friend's soft profile bathed in the evening glow, her voice gentling a little:

"Sure, I passed! Still, back then, whenever I ran into Shiori in the hallway—no matter how many classmates were crowding around asking her questions, whether she'd just finished an 800-meter fitness run or had a low-grade cold—her back was always ramrod straight, her headband sat immaculate to the millimeter, and if anyone asked whether she was tired, she'd always smile and say, 'Not at all, I can handle something like this on my own.'"
Reaching out a finger, Ayako pointed lightly toward the deep burgundy velvet headband Fujisaki wore today, blinking with a warm smile:

"That's why spending three weeks here at the hospital has felt so wonderfully surreal to me. Being a doctor has to be ten times busier than being a student ever was, yet the Shiori of today doesn't just zone out in front of caramel pudding and strawberry panna cotta—when she's tired, she can casually tell someone, 'I'll slack off a little today and leave the rest to you.'"
Shiori Fujisaki's fingers stilled lightly around her teacup.

Outside the glass gallery, the evening breeze stirred the courtyard tree shadows. She lowered her lashes to look into the clear amber tea in her cup, then lifted her gaze a moment later—carrying a little less of her usual poised restraint, and a quiet, candid tenderness in its place:
"...Back then, I always felt as though answering even a single question less than flawlessly—or letting anyone catch sight of me struggling—meant letting down everyone's expectations."
As she spoke, her gaze brushed naturally across the table over Ryuji Sakaguchi, a faint curve warming her lips:

"It took working in a hospital for me to slowly realize that neither an operating table nor a ward is a place one person can hold up alone just by scoring a hundred out of a hundred. When there's someone beside you whom you trust to take the baton for the next leg, letting your shoulders drop a little isn't such a bad thing at all."
"Staying wound up at 100% is exhausting—slacking off half a page now and then is just right."
"Sounds like student-era Dr. Fujisaki was way harder to approach than she is now."

"Staying wound tight at a hundred points nonstop really is exhausting. In a place like Hoshimi where curveballs fly every day, knowing when to slack off for half a page is probably the mark of a truly seasoned attending physician."
Shiori Fujisaki's eyes curved softly as she answered in a quiet voice:
"Mm... With Dr. Sakaguchi's stamp of approval, I'll feel completely justified slacking off every once in a while from now on."
Looking at the soft burgundy velvet headband resting in her hair, Ryuji Sakaguchi chuckled lightly in mild teasing:
"Hearing it put like that, if I'd known Dr. Fujisaki back in school, I probably wouldn't even have worked up the nerve to ask to borrow her notes."
Shiori Fujisaki shot him a gentle mock glare, though her eyes brimmed with amusement:

"I wasn't nearly as intimidating as Ayako makes me sound. If it had been you asking to borrow them, Dr. Sakaguchi, at most I would've... reminded you to use a bookmark instead of dog-earing the corners."

Taking in the effortless rapport flowing back and forth between the two of them, Ayako Katagiri tactfully refrained from teasing them out loud—simply tipping her head back with a grin to finish the last warm sip of black tea, picking up her sketchbook, and smoothing down her skirt as she stood:

"All righty—tea mooched, old stories aired! While the second-floor outpatient hallway is empty before six, I'm gonna go grab two quick dusk light-and-shadow sketches, so I'll get out of your hair and let you two wrap up for the day!"
Shiori Fujisaki rose along with her to add a gentle reminder:
"It'll be dark soon, so head back to your lodgings early once you finish sketching—don't crouch by a stairwell drawing until you forget dinner again."
Ayako Katagiri gave them both a breezy wave:
"Don't worry! This giant-badge Research Observer clocks out right on time—see you tomorrow!"
Her high silvery-violet ponytail and white nurse cap bobbed merrily out of sight around the bend of the gallery.
Once Ayako's brisk footsteps faded completely, only Ryuji Sakaguchi and Shiori Fujisaki remained in the hushed glass courtyard corridor.

Shiori Fujisaki let out a soft breath, and the poised composure she had maintained before her old friend finally melted into a delicate flush that crept all the way to the fair tips of her ears. Stepping half a pace closer to Sakaguchi's side, she murmured helplessly:

"...Honestly, Ayako's manga-artist eyes are a little too sharp for comfort. When she stared at me saying 'you actually know how to slack off now,' for a second I nearly thought she'd seen right through us."
Picking up her stack of follow-up folders from the table for her, Ryuji Sakaguchi chuckled quietly:

"You handled it calmly enough—she probably chalked it up to ordinary coworker teamwork. Once I finish signing off on that half-page consult note, want me to wait for you at the street corner outside the main gate so we can walk back together?"
Shiori Fujisaki looked up at him, the warm sunset reflected in her clear eyes as her lips curved into a tender smile reserved solely for unguarded moments:
"...Mm. Then please wrap up that signature quickly—I'll go get changed first and wait for you."
Watching Ayako disappear down the hall, Shiori Fujisaki gathered the teacups neatly onto the tray and turned toward Ryuji Sakaguchi with a fresh, gentle smile:
"Sorry you had to sit through that, Dr. Sakaguchi. Whenever I run into an old friend from school, we end up reminiscing over silly little things before I know it."
Ryuji Sakaguchi shook his head, lifting the lab recheck summary sheet in his hand:

"Not at all—it's a rare treat hearing stories from honor-student Dr. Fujisaki's school days. I'll head back up to the third floor to finish signing that consult note, so go ahead and call it an early night."
Shiori Fujisaki gave a poised, gentle nod:
"Mm—thank you for all your hard work today. See you tomorrow."
Before anyone knew it, the thirty-day hospital research residency had entered its final week.

At five-thirty that evening, when Ryuji Sakaguchi, Kaori Miyama, and Shiori Fujisaki arrived at the doctors' lounge as promised, the table wasn't covered in wild character doodles like two weeks earlier. Instead, a single stack of B4 manga storyboard drafts sat neatly fastened with a binder clip.

For once, Ayako Katagiri didn't wave them over with boisterous fanfare. She stood with her hands behind her back, fingers lightly twisting the hem of her skirt, wearing the nervous expression of a student about to hand in an exam paper:

"Dr. Sakaguchi, Dr. Miyama, Shiori... This week I sifted through all several hundred pages of sketches from my first twenty-odd days here, pulled three all-nighters, and finally finished the 32-page official storyboard draft for Chapter 1 of 'Tales of Hoshimi Hospital.'"
She nudged the stack of storyboards half an inch forward and took a deep breath:
"Before I mail it off to my editor for review, I wanted to ask the three of you to be my very first readers!"
Standing by the table, Kaori Miyama folded her arms, her expression as calm as still water, as though she had already braced herself for anything:

"...Before I open it, let me confirm one thing. Page one starts right off with the surgical lights snapping on and some poor soul lying bewildered on the operating table getting their belly sliced open in a lurid spectacle, doesn't it? Fair warning: even if you drew me as a Demon Queen cleaving open a treasure chest, if the anatomical orientation is off, I'm still going to nitpick it."
Ayako Katagiri burst into a giggle:
"Just open it and take a look first, Dr. Miyama! There'll be plenty of time to nitpick after you read it!"

Ryuji Sakaguchi picked up the stack of storyboards, still carrying the faint scent of pencil lead and eraser shavings, and turned to the first page as Kaori Miyama and Shiori Fujisaki leaned in beside him.
There were no surgical lights, no scalpels, and no sensational close-ups anywhere in sight.
Page one of the storyboard held only a few quiet, clean establishing panels of early morning—

At six-thirty in the morning, as the first pale light of dawn touched the horizon, the night lights along the hospital corridor clicked off one by one. At the third-floor nurses' station, night-shift and morning-shift nurses murmured over the handover board to cross-check drainage logs, the pockets of their white nurse dresses stuffed full with three-color ballpoint pens, medical tape, and pocket-watch chains peeking out.
Turning to pages two and three—

The scene cut to a vending machine around the corner of the corridor. A young dark-haired female doctor who had just survived the back half of an ER night shift stood alone in the morning light—not a single comical icicle drawn above her head—eyelids lowered slightly, one hand gently rubbing the aching bridge of her brow while the other pressed the button for "Hot Canned Black Coffee," a thin wisp of white steam rising from the opened tab.
Kaori Miyama's gaze settled on those two quiet panels of that familiar figure from behind, and the critiques waiting on the tip of her tongue abruptly died away.
Shiori Fujisaki gently turned through the next several pages, warm surprise rising in her eyes:
"Ah... this panel is the first-floor lobby entrance."

Pages four and five depicted the hospital's main entrance bathed in ten-o'clock morning sunshine: a young woman who had just completed her discharge paperwork walked up to the revolving doors carrying her travel bag, then suddenly turned around to wave an emphatic goodbye to the nurse and young male doctor seeing her off beside the reception desk; nearby, half a yawning head poked out of the pharmacy window; in the second-floor lounge, two female doctors politely insisted the other take the last caramel pudding in the dessert machine; and down at the end of the hall, two razor-sharp attending surgeons each holding a cup of coffee gave a slight nod as they passed one another.
Small, warm, and threaded with dry humor that brought a knowing smile—just like the countless ordinary hours that truly flowed through Hoshimi Hospital every single day.
Not until two-thirds of the way through the chapter did the emergency hotline suddenly ring—

Across a dramatic two-page spread, the automatic doors of the surgical wing slid apart and the main overhead surgical lights blazed to life. The very doctors and nurses who moments ago had been rubbing their brows at the vending machine or sipping black tea in the lounge put on their scrub caps and surgical masks to take their places around the operating table—and in that instant, every trace of drowsiness and fatigue vanished, leaving every pair of eyes above those masks breathtakingly calm, sharp, and dependable.

And on the final page of Chapter 1, with the operation safely concluded and city lights twinkling beyond the corridor windows, several pairs of hands freshly stripped of sterile gloves gathered once again in front of the vending machine.
Silence hung in the lounge for several seconds.
Ryuji Sakaguchi closed the final page of the storyboard draft and looked up at Ayako Katagiri across the table:

"...That really surprised me, Ms. Katagiri. Going by standard commercial serialization formulas, I figured you'd put the most bizarre surgical mishap in the first five pages to hook readers right away."
Ayako Katagiri sheepishly scratched her cheek, the nurse cap atop her head bobbing slightly:
"To tell the truth, on my very first day here, all I knew was that drawing sensational surgeries alone wouldn't cut it—I still had no idea how Chapter 1 should actually open."
She looked down at the stack of pages reworked in pencil again and again, her eyes curving into gentle crescents as she spoke softly:

"But after wandering these halls in this uniform for nearly a month—watching everyone get up early for shift handovers, scramble for hot coffee, and quietly fret over patients behind the scenes—it suddenly hit me while I was sketching. Masterful scalpel work in the OR is super cool, of course, and ridiculous mix-ups are hilarious, too, but if I open with nothing but spectacle, readers will never know what wonderfully fascinating, living, breathing people are standing behind those surgical masks."
She lifted her head and met the gazes of all three with a radiant smile:

"I want to show everyone that morning can of hot coffee and the three-color pen in a nurse's pocket first. Once readers fall in love with the oddballs who inhabit this hospital, won't the stories on the operating table make their hearts race even harder and keep their eyes glued to the page?"
"It really captures the spirit of Hoshimi Hospital. Much more compelling than just drawing bizarre surgeries."
"That panel on page three rubbing her brow in front of the vending machine is especially spot-on."
Ryuji Sakaguchi squared up the stack of storyboards neatly and handed it back to her with a warm, assured nod:
"It really captures the spirit of Hoshimi Hospital. Compared to opening with a lurid surgery for shock value, a lively, grounded beginning like this holds up far better."
Ayako Katagiri's eyes lit up and she pumped her fist:
"Awesome! If even the ever-composed Dr. Sakaguchi says so, I can pitch this to my editor with total confidence!"
Ryuji Sakaguchi tapped page three of the storyboard with a faint smile:

"That panel on page three—buying black coffee at the vending machine while rubbing her brow—captures her demeanor with uncanny precision. Looks like you've been sneaking plenty of sketches of a certain someone coming off night shift."
The tips of Kaori Miyama's ears twitched almost imperceptibly; she gave a quiet cough and looked away, yet for once voiced no protest.
Smiling, Shiori Fujisaki lightly brushed her fingertips across the title "Tales of Hoshimi Hospital" on the cover sheet:
"The pacing feels wonderful, Ayako. By the time I finished the last page, even the hallways I walk to work every day felt a little more endearing."
Ayako Katagiri stole a cautious glance at Kaori Miyama, who still hadn't said a word:
"U-Um... what do you think, Dr. Miyama? I didn't get the team positioning or instrument angles wrong in the OR panels this time, did I?"
Kaori Miyama looked down at the stack of storyboards on the table, paused for two seconds, and let her ordinarily sharp, critical brow soften ever so slightly:
"...On page twenty-four, the wrist angle of the first assistant holding the retractor is slightly too high. Lower it five degrees when you ink it and it'll be fine."
Ayako Katagiri had barely let out a breath of relief:
Kaori Miyama raised her eyes to meet hers, the corners of her lips curving upward by the faintest fraction:
"As for the remaining thirty-one pages... they're very well drawn. Much more respectable than that four-panel strip with the empty treasure chest last time, at least."
Ayako Katagiri blinked for half a second, then beamed so wide she nearly bounced off the floor:
"Lucky—!! I got Dr. Miyama's stamp of approval!!"
In the blink of an eye, the final day of the thirty-day hospital research residency had arrived.

When Ryuji Sakaguchi, Kaori Miyama, and Shiori Fujisaki accompanied Ayako Katagiri back into the Director's Office, all three felt strangely unaccustomed to the sight of her. After a full month of watching her dart up and down the corridors in a nurse cap, seeing Ayako back in a lavender casual cardigan and slacks with her silver-violet high ponytail uncovered took a moment to register.
Holding a neatly packed rectangular white gift box in both hands, Ayako Katagiri set it squarely on Asuka Shiromiya's desk.

With the lid resting open, inside lay the Hoshimi Hospital nurse dress and cap she had worn for an entire month—hand-washed snow-white and crisp, every single pleat carefully ironed and folded—and centered right atop the pristine collar sat that spotless custom badge, a full size larger than standard issue: "Ayako Katagiri | Manga Artist / Research Observer | [NO MEDICAL PROCEDURES PERMITTED]."
Ayako Katagiri took half a step back and offered Asuka Shiromiya a solemn bow:

"Director Shiromiya! My thirty-day research residency officially wraps up today! Over this past month, I didn't wander into any restricted zones, didn't touch a single medical instrument, and didn't lose a single organ—I've washed, ironed, and brought back the borrowed uniform and badge! Thank you so very much for the hospital's care this whole month!"

Asuka Shiromiya glanced down at the uniform folded with military precision inside the box, an amused smile playing at her lips. Instead of taking it, however, she reached out with slender fingers and gently slid the entire box—oversized badge and all—right back in front of Ayako.
"...Eh? Director Shiromiya, did I miss a spot washing it?"
Asuka Shiromiya shook her head and spoke with a warm smile:

"You washed it beautifully—not even the collar shaping lost its form, which shows how well you treasured it. Still, this outfit was tailored specifically to your measurements from the start. Along with this custom badge, please keep them both as mementos, Ms. Katagiri."
Ayako Katagiri's eyes flew wide open:
"F-For me to keep?! Both the uniform AND this giant badge?!"
Resting her chin atop folded hands, Asuka Shiromiya gave a playful wink tinged with her signature dry wit:

"You've only just finalized the storyboards for Chapter 1, after all. Once you're back in your studio drawing serialized manuscripts, if you get stuck at two in the morning on how a nurse skirt pleats or where the cap pins sit, we can hardly have you knocking on Dr. Fujisaki's window to pose for you, can we? Hanging the uniform on a studio rack as a live reference—and keeping this '[NO MEDICAL PROCEDURES PERMITTED]' badge on your desk as a deadline good-luck charm—sounds like quite the bargain, wouldn't you say?"
Beside her, Kaori Miyama added evenly:

"One ground rule has to be set in stone up front, though. That uniform stays on a hanger in your studio strictly for reference—you are never to wear it to another hospital for research. Otherwise, when another hospital calls Hoshimi to verify your credentials, we'll be stuck explaining why a nurse's badge says '[NO MEDICAL PROCEDURES PERMITTED].'"
"I doubt you'd find a second badge like it in any hospital in Japan."

Ayako Katagiri carefully closed the lid and hugged the box—together with the oversized badge that had accompanied her for thirty full days—tightly against her chest, a faint shimmer catching in her eyes before she broke into a huge, unclouded smile:
"That's amazing—!! I swear I'll hang it right beside my drawing desk as a family heirloom! Thank you so much, Director Shiromiya!!"

Once her visitor sign-out was complete, Sakaguchi, Miyama, and Fujisaki walked Ayako Katagiri—oversized portfolio slung across her back and uniform gift box cradled in her arms—all the way out through the glass main doors on the ground floor of Hoshimi Hospital.
Outside, the sky stretched clear and bright, a gentle breeze rustling the tidy row of street trees in front of the hospital.

Ayako Katagiri hopped down two steps, turned around to face the three white-coated doctors seeing her off, took half a step backward, and shaded her brow to gaze up at the Hoshimi Hospital sign with a wistful sigh:

"Whoa... To think, the first time I was discharged through these doors, I was clutching my freshly stitched belly thinking, 'I've probably used up my lifetime quota of hospital visits.' And yet now that my month is up, I'm actually sad to leave!"
Shiori Fujisaki stepped forward and, just as whenever she saw an old friend off at the station, gently smoothed down a lock of silver-violet hair tousled by the breeze:

"You'll be heading into full serialization prep now, right? Knowing your old habit of forgetting clocks exist the moment you start inking manuscripts, even without a '[NO MEDICAL PROCEDURES PERMITTED]' badge on your chest, promise you'll eat and sleep on time. Next time we meet, let's have afternoon tea at a cafe outside—no checking in through the ER allowed, okay?"
Grinning from ear to ear, Ayako Katagiri flashed an "OK" sign:
"Aye-aye, Dr. Fujisaki! The second Chapter 1's publication date is locked in, you'll be the very first to get my message!"
With that, she turned her gaze toward Kaori Miyama standing nearby and gave a teasing wink:
"Guess you finally won't have to worry about me lurking around the fourth-floor corridor every day anymore, huh, Dr. Miyama?"
Meeting her gaze, Kaori Miyama didn't furrow her brow like she had on day one. Instead, she stood straight and spoke in her usual calm, crisp tone:

"It'll certainly be quieter. ...Still, since the title on your storyboard carries the name 'Hoshimi Hospital,' when you get to drawing ER triage or instrument details at the operating table, if anything is unclear, you have permission to message Sakaguchi and me—either through Dr. Fujisaki or directly."
"Eh? You're willing to be my off-site medical consultant, Dr. Miyama?!"
Kaori Miyama shifted her gaze half an inch aside with a quiet huff:
"I simply have no desire to see hemostats drawn like kitchen shears in a shojo manga magazine, tarnishing our surgical department's professional reputation by association."
Glancing fondly at his sharp-tongued, soft-hearted partner, Ryuji Sakaguchi extended a hand toward Ayako with a warm smile:

"Take care on your way home, Ms. Katagiri. Best of luck with the serialization of 'Tales of Hoshimi Hospital'—and once the collected volume goes to print, remember to save a signed copy for our hospital book corner."
Ayako Katagiri gave Sakaguchi's hand a hearty shake, beaming with vibrant energy:

"It's a deal! Once I've drawn everyone's stories, I'll come right back in person holding a fresh-off-the-press copy for a launch party! Well then—Dr. Sakaguchi, Dr. Miyama, Shiori—I'm off into seclusion to draw my manuscripts! Goodbye—!!"

Hugging the white box with the nurse uniform and oversized badge tightly to her chest, the twenty-five-year-old manga artist spun around and merged into the bustling street beyond the gates with steps light as the wind.
