Watching that spirited figure disappear down the avenue, Kaori Miyama let out a quiet breath and glanced at her wristwatch:
"...Come on, back to the ward. We still have two observation cases to handle this afternoon."
A gentle smile lingered on Shiori Fujisaki's lips:
"Yes—the hospital will be settling right back into its usual rhythm."
Ryuji Sakaguchi cast one last look across the sunlit lobby humming quietly with daily life, then turned to walk side by side with his two dependable partners back down the hall.

The curtain had fallen on Ayako Katagiri's thirty-day hospital residency—while on the other side of the city, the first true pen stroke of a brand-new manuscript titled "Tales of Hoshimi Hospital" was only just touching paper.

At two in the afternoon, Ryuji Sakaguchi had just stepped out of the second-floor dressing room when he spotted a familiar figure in white standing by the corridor window ahead.

Dressed in a crisp white nurse dress and traditional white nurse cap, Ayako Katagiri had her back to the walkway, head bowed over a hardcover sketchbook as she roughed in the window frame at the end of the hall. Judging solely by the tailored fit and neatly pinned brim, she looked every inch a young nurse double-checking patient charts.
Just then, a female patient with a mild case stepped out of a nearby ward wearing a knit cardigan, caught sight of Ayako from behind, and called out:
"Um, excuse me, Nurse—is the automated payment kiosk on the first floor to the left of the reception desk?"
Ryuji Sakaguchi opened his mouth to step in on Ayako's behalf, only to see Ayako Katagiri jolt and whirl around with battle-honed half-second reflexes—

First, she clapped her right hand firmly over her own mouth and clicked her heels together at attention; next, the index and middle fingers of her left hand pointed straight at the red-on-white acrylic badge on her left chest, a full size larger than standard issue!
Only after confirming the patient had clearly read the bold bottom line—"[NO MEDICAL PROCEDURES PERMITTED]"—did Ayako lower her hand from her mouth and flash a radiant, textbook-polite smile:

"Reporting in! I'm not a real nurse—I'm Ayako Katagiri, a Research Observer here drawing a manga! For hospital directions and consultation questions, though, please ask the genuine article right behind you—Dr. Sakaguchi!"
The patient blinked, took in the unmistakably oversized badge, and turned to see Ryuji Sakaguchi walking up, breaking into an amused laugh.
Suppressing a smile, Ryuji Sakaguchi gestured warmly toward the elevators:
"The automated payment kiosk is ten meters to the right once you exit the first-floor lobby elevator, right next to the reception desk."
"Ah, got it—thank you, Dr. Sakaguchi! And thank you too, lovely Ms. Manga Artist."
After watching the smiling patient step into the elevator, Ryuji Sakaguchi glanced back at Ayako, who was still standing half at attention:
"...That cover-your-mouth-and-point-at-the-badge combo just now—have you been practicing that in secret?"
Ayako Katagiri puffed up proudly and flicked the oversized badge on her chest:

"Of course! Ever since the first day I put this uniform on, I practiced twenty reps in front of the mirror—cover my mouth first so I don't blurt out medical answers, then flash the badge and state my name! My last lesson from casually chatting with someone in a hospital corridor was way too painful, so now my badge-draw speed is faster than my storyboarding hand!"
Ryuji Sakaguchi gave an approving nod:
"If Director Shiromiya saw that performance, she'd probably be so touched she'd award you a Model Visitor banner."
Grinning, Ayako Katagiri flipped open her sketchbook:
"I'll pass on the banner—first let me jot down 'The One Second I Was Almost Mistaken for a Real Nurse' for a four-panel gag!"
Danger Sense in the Gynecology Corridor

Passing through the second-floor gynecology corridor, Ryuji Sakaguchi spotted Ayako Katagiri from afar tiptoeing flush against the opposite wall, keeping a cautious three-meter safety buffer as she sketched a perspective study of the "Gynecological Exam Room" doorplate.
Ryuji Sakaguchi walked over and stopped beside her:
"Why are you sketching from all the way back here? Don't you usually love leaning right up close to inspect details?"
The nurse cap atop Ayako Katagiri's head gave a tiny shiver as she lowered her voice conspiratorially:
"You don't understand, Dr. Sakaguchi—manga artists have wild-animal instincts! The aura radiating from behind that door keeps reminding me of that ice-cold operating table six months ago..."
Before she even finished speaking, the door to the gynecological exam room swung briskly open from the inside!

Gynecology Chief Aqua Mizuki breezed out carrying a sterile-draped stainless-steel instrument tray, her bright azure hair bouncing with each lively step. The moment she looked up and spotted a young woman in a white nurse uniform across the hall, Chief Mizuki's eyes lit right up:

"Ooh? Are you the new nurse rotating in this week? Perfect timing! I just finished sterilizing a bivalve speculum and uterine sound set, and I needed someone to help test the new illumination angle on the exam lamp—oh, Sakaguchi's here too! Come take a look together!"

As the chilly metallic glint off the instruments flashed across her vision, every hair on Ayako Katagiri's body stood on end. She zipped straight behind Ryuji Sakaguchi's back, thrusting her oversized badge forward with both hands as far as her arms could reach:
"N-Not a new nurse!! Please read the red print, Chief Mizuki—I'm a Research Observer who draws shojo manga! No medical procedures permitted! And serving as a live teaching aid is EXTRA forbidden!!"
Aqua Mizuki blinked her wide eyes, leaned half a step closer to read the badge, and let out a dawning "Ohhh—!":

"So you're the resident manga artist Asuka approved! Why didn't you say so? If you're drawing a hospital series, how could you stop at sketching the doorplate outside? Want to come observe my signature modified-lithotomy instrument-exposure aesthetics? The line tension would look incredible in a two-page spread!"
Ayako Katagiri shook her head so frantically her silver-violet ponytail whipped back and forth like a rattle drum:
"My series runs in an all-ages shojo manga magazine!! If I draw a two-page spread like that, the editor-in-chief will cancel my serialization tomorrow morning!!"
Right on cue, Ryuji Sakaguchi stepped calmly between the two without batting an eye:
"Spare her serialization, Chief Mizuki. If you actually pull her into your exam room, Director Shiromiya will have to convene another incident review meeting tonight."
Aqua Mizuki puffed out her cheeks in disappointment:
"Aw, come on, it was a perfectly serious anatomical perspective reference..."
Using Sakaguchi as visual cover, Ayako Katagiri clutched her sketchbook tight and sidestepped at breakneck crab-walk speed all the way to the corner of the hall:
"I owe you my life, Dr. Sakaguchi! I've got the gynecology corridor exterior down, so I'm making a tactical retreat—!!"
At five-thirty in the evening, a demanding, hours-long emergency surgery wrapped up smoothly.

Back in their white coats, Ryuji Sakaguchi and Kaori Miyama walked side by side out of the fourth-floor changing passage, heading by unspoken routine toward the vending machine around the corner. After several hours of unbroken concentration, Miyama didn't say a word, eyelids lowered slightly out of habit while the thumb and index finger of her right hand opened and closed almost imperceptibly at her side.
Just past the potted foliage plant at the corner, both of them stopped in their tracks.
Curled into a compact ball on a low stool beside the planter sat Ayako Katagiri in her white nurse cap, sketchbook open across her knees, her pencil rustling swiftly over the page.
With a slight furrow of her brow, Kaori Miyama stepped over and stood diagonally in front of her:
"...Ms. Katagiri. What are you doing crouched behind a potted plant outside the surgical wing?"
Startled, Ayako Katagiri looked up, spotted the pair, and hastily pressed her palms together with an apologetic grin:
"Ah, Dr. Miyama, Dr. Sakaguchi—great work on your surgery! I didn't cross the fourth-floor yellow line, promise! Right here is the lounge corridor's legal observation zone!"
Kaori Miyama eyed the sketchbook in her hands, her gaze sharpening:
"What were you staring at us and drawing just now? If you put ice cubes on top of my head again—"
Without hesitation, Ayako Katagiri flipped the sketchbook around and held it up for both of them to see:
"It's not a gag doodle at all! I'm drawing 'The Genuine Unwinding Moment Within Five Minutes of Surgeons Stepping Off the Table'!"
Ryuji Sakaguchi looked down in mild surprise.

There wasn't a trace of caricature on the page—only clean, restrained pencil lines: in the slanting evening light of the hallway, two young doctors in white coats walked toward a vending machine; the dark-haired woman half a step ahead carried a faint weight in her shoulders, her right hand hanging at her side unconsciously repeating the subtle motion of releasing a hemostat ratchet, while the male doctor trailing just behind already had coins ready in his palm.
Staring at that unmistakable detail of her own right hand captured on paper, Kaori Miyama blinked in momentary stillness.
Ayako Katagiri rubbed the tip of her nose bashfully:

"Because I noticed that during those few dozen seconds right after Dr. Miyama steps out of the OR—before she presses the coffee button—she looks different from her usual frosty self. There's something really cool about seeing someone who just gave everything they had..."
The pale tip of Kaori Miyama's ear twitched faintly; she turned away at once toward the vending machine, her voice returning to its customary flatness:
"...Stop wasting lead on pointless little tics."

After two cans dropped into the slot, Miyama bent down to retrieve two hot drinks—handing a hot black coffee to Ryuji Sakaguchi beside her before walking back past the low stool and setting a warm can of corn potage lightly on the corner of Ayako's sketchbook.
Without looking back, Kaori Miyama headed toward the elevator, leaving behind only a brusque reminder:
"There's a cold draft near the corridor vent. Don't forget your own abdomen went under the knife six months ago—once you're done sketching, go sit somewhere warm in the lounge."
Ryuji Sakaguchi smiled at Ayako as she cradled the warm can looking deeply touched:
"Drink it while it's hot. You don't get an honorarium tip from Dr. Miyama every day."
A Corridor with Built-In Background Lightning
Just past nine in the morning, bright sunlight streamed down the main third-floor surgical corridor.

Walking down the middle of the hall with his morning ward-round clipboard, Ryuji Sakaguchi spotted Ayako Katagiri standing dutifully beside the bulletin board mapping out a floor-flow diagram. Seeing Sakaguchi approach, Ayako raised her pencil with a smile to wave—
At the far end of the corridor, the double glass doors swung open and two unmistakable figures strode forward side by side.

On the left, Chief Surgeon Emiko Mido cut a tall, commanding figure, the hem of her white coat lifting crisply with each stride; on the right, Deputy Chief Artoria Pendragon stood only 154 centimeters tall, yet carried her spine straight as an unsheathed sword, pale-gold braids pinned neatly behind her head and her trademark cowlick unyielding in the morning light.
"For Thursday morning's partial hepatectomy, assign scrub nurses to Class-I major surgery standards. I won't accept last-minute rookies."
"The roster was finalized last night, Dr. Mido. Provided the lead surgeon completes her pre-op sign-off on time before eight-twenty, staff handoffs won't slip by a single minute."
Emiko Mido let out a cool huff:
"Worry about your own complex consultation this afternoon first, Deputy Chief."

Although both kept their voices impeccably poised and measured, two young residents and a junior nurse passing along the hall reacted as though sensing an approaching high-pressure weather front, flattening themselves neatly against opposite walls to clear the way.
Instinctively holding her breath, Ayako Katagiri stepped back beside the bulletin board alongside Ryuji Sakaguchi.
As the pair drew near, their footsteps slowed briefly. Emiko Mido gave Ryuji Sakaguchi a composed nod:

Artoria returned Sakaguchi's greeting with a crisp nod of her own, then turned her clear emerald eyes toward Ayako Katagiri beside him. Her gaze lingered on the top of Ayako's head for half a second before she offered an earnest, gentle reminder:
"Good morning, Ms. Katagiri. The bobby pin securing the right side of your nurse cap has slipped out half a centimeter—it may slide off while you look down to sketch, so remember to refasten it."
Clapping both hands to her cap, Ayako Katagiri snapped to attention on the spot:
"Yes, ma'am!! Thank you for the heads-up, Deputy Chief Pendragon!!"

Not until the two surgical powerhouses disappeared around the far end of the corridor did Ayako Katagiri refasten her hairpin and clutch her sketchbook, eyes starry as she exclaimed to Ryuji Sakaguchi:

"W-What incredible presence...! Did you see everyone part to both sides automatically just now, Dr. Sakaguchi?! Whenever I put the two of them in the same panel, I won't even need mood screentones—the air in the hallway practically crackles with lightning all on its own!"
Glancing down the now-peaceful hallway, Ryuji Sakaguchi chuckled:
"That's everyday morning scenery in Hoshimi's surgical department. You'll get used to it, Ms. Katagiri."
At five past five in the evening, hardly any patients remained in the first-floor outpatient lobby.

On his way to the pharmacy window to verify a postoperative analgesia-pump prescription, Ryuji Sakaguchi spotted Ayako Katagiri in her white nurse cap leaning halfway across the dispensing counter, palms pressed together as she pleaded with pharmacist Manami Iimura inside:

"Pretty please, Ms. Iimura! Just teach me one or two emergency drug names that run over a dozen syllables long and sound super esoteric and cool! You know—the kind in medical dramas where the male lead waves his hand in a crisis and shouts, 'Push five milligrams of such-and-such, stat!' and instantly commands the whole room!"

Inside the window, twenty-three-year-old Manami Iimura peeled off her compounding gloves at an unhurried pace, propped her cheek on one hand as she smiled at the devout manga artist before her, and shot an amused sidelong glance toward the approaching Ryuji Sakaguchi:
"Well now, speak of our leading man! Dr. Sakaguchi, when you're running a code at the operating table, do you go out of your way to shout ten-word tongue-twister chemical names just to look cool?"
Handing the prescription slip through the window, Ryuji Sakaguchi calmly burst her bubble:

"If I ever shouted an obscure full chemical name during an emergency surgery, the circulating nurse would assume I was hypoxic and delirious. The more urgent the situation, the shorter and clearer the standard generic name has to be."
"Ugh... So shouting ultra-long spell-like drug names actually outs you as an amateur..."
Manami Iimura let out a soft laugh, stamped Sakaguchi's prescription slip, and leaned slightly forward across the counter, lowering her voice to tease Ayako:

"Speaking of medication experiences, though, don't you already have firsthand material of your own, Ms. Katagiri? That pre-op intravenous sedative six months ago was dispensed right from my window, you know—word has it you were nodding off in a daze while complimenting how pretty the OR lights looked?"
Ayako Katagiri flushed crimson all the way up to the brim of her nurse cap:
"Waaah—!! How does even Ms. Iimura down in Pharmacy know mortifying details like that?!"

Eyes crinkling with mirth, Manami Iimura lifted a pastry box from beneath the counter—freshly picked up by a coworker—and pressed two individually wrapped crispy cream puffs into Ayako's and Sakaguchi's hands:

"Just teasing—that's what happens when Ms. Katagiri is a hospital-wide celebrity. Here, consider this hush money. Eat them while the shells are still crisp, because I'm locking up the window right on the dot!"
Watching Manami briskly pull down the window blinds to clock out, Ayako Katagiri blinked over the cream puff in her palms and turned to Sakaguchi in admiration:
"...She totally exposed my dark history, and yet I love her personality too!"

Just after lunch break, Ayako Katagiri sat cross-legged on the end of a corridor bench scratching her head over a rough sketch of a mercury sphygmomanometer, a tiny pile of eraser shavings already gathered beside her knee:

"Weird... When the cuff wraps around the upper arm, does the rubber air tube exit along the inside of the elbow, or loop down from the top...? Drawing medical gear is way harder than drawing fantasy magic wands..."
Passing by after checking a nursing cart, eighteen-year-old rookie nurse Moe Honjo overheard her, paused, and shyly peeked over at the page:

"U-Um... Ms. Katagiri, for an upper-arm blood pressure reading, the lower edge of the cuff sits two to three centimeters above the antecubital fossa, and the rubber tubing runs downward along the medial side over the brachial artery..."
Ayako Katagiri's head snapped up, gripping her pencil as if she'd just spotted a lifesaver:
"Really?! You know your stuff inside and out, Ms. Honjo!"
Cheeks coloring faintly, Moe Honjo waved her hands modestly and pulled a palm-sized spiral memo pad—its spine worn fuzzy from constant flipping—out of her nurse-dress pocket:
"Not at all! When I first started here, I mixed up tubing directions all the time too... See, I only memorized them after drawing tons of little diagrams in my notebook."

Ayako Katagiri leaned in for a look, and her eyes went wide at once—Moe's tiny nursing pocketbook bristled with red, yellow, and blue index tabs, packed not only with arrow-annotated stick diagrams of blood-pressure cuffs and three-way IV stopcocks, but also neat, earnest little reminders in the margins like "Never make the patient feel scared!"
Looking down at her own thick sketchbook bristling with colorful sticky notes, then back up at the shy, earnest Moe Honjo, Ayako felt an instant surge of cross-disciplinary camaraderie:
"Ms. Honjo!! That's unmistakably the notebook of a comrade-in-arms!!"
Walking down the hall alongside Ryuji Sakaguchi just then, Hiroko Sugimura spotted the two heads bent together comparing notes, a warm smile touching her lips:
"Here I was wondering why Moe took forever bringing back a clipboard—turns out she found a kindred spirit."
Catching sight of Sakaguchi and Hiroko, Moe Honjo flushed to the tips of her ears and scrambled to her feet:
"M-Ms. Sugimura, Dr. Sakaguchi! I wasn't slacking off—I was just showing Ms. Katagiri how the cuff folds..."
Summoning her courage, Moe rolled her left sleeve up slightly and demonstrated the cuff alignment in midair for Ayako:
"I-If you fold the edge flat like this, it won't pinch the patient's skin."
Ryuji Sakaguchi gave an encouraging nod:
"Textbook explanation. Looks like you've remembered every single detail Hiroko taught you."

Praised directly by Sakaguchi, Moe Honjo ducked her head with bright, shining eyes and murmured a quiet "Yes!"; beside her, Ayako Katagiri polished off the cuff angle in ten brisk seconds of pencil strokes and threw up a satisfied thumbs-up:
"Jackpot on the details! Thank you, Instructor Moe, and thank you, Ms. Sugimura!"
The Best Models for Dynamic Uniform Folds
Around three in the afternoon, clear daylight poured down the west corridor of the inpatient wing.

Passing the supply room carrying two archived chart binders, Ryuji Sakaguchi saw Rumi Iwasaki and Shiori Yoneda just wheeling out a freshly counted linen cart when Ayako Katagiri politely flagged them down with sketchbook in hand.

"Sorry to bother you for two minutes! I'm practicing 'the dynamic skirt folds of a nurse turning in the hall to hand over a chart clipboard'—would either of you mind doing a half-turn on the spot so I can catch a drapery reference?"
Ever outgoing and spirited, Rumi Iwasaki lit up at once, hugged her clipboard to her chest, and struck a brisk, photogenic mid-turn handover pose:
"Easy as pie—leave it to me! How's this turning angle, Ms. Katagiri, camera-ready enough? Want Dr. Sakaguchi to pose receiving the clipboard while we're at it?"
Stopping a couple of paces away, Ryuji Sakaguchi smiled:
"Count me out of the frame—Rumi's energy alone is plenty to fill the whole panel."
Beside her, Shiori Yoneda watched Rumi beaming in the sunlight with sparkling eyes, then noticed what Rumi's sweeping spin had knocked askew and blurted out:
"Ah, wait a second! Big Sis Rumi, your left collar tucked inward a tiny bit, and your nurse cap shifted a hair—"
Realizing the instant the words left her mouth that Dr. Sakaguchi and a guest were standing right there, eighteen-year-old Shiori Yoneda turned bright red and stammered to correct herself:
"I-I mean Ms. Iwasaki! Excuse me, let me smooth that out for you!"
Rumi Iwasaki laughed heartily without a care in the world, letting Shiori rise half an inch onto her tiptoes to fuss over her collar and cap brim until both sat picture-perfect:
"What's there to be shy about? Dr. Sakaguchi isn't a stranger, and that's what you call me off duty anyway! Come on, Shiori, stand right next to me—a two-shot is way livelier!"
Ears glowing red, Shiori Yoneda nodded and stepped dutifully half a pace beside Rumi, hugging her clipboard primly.

Across from them, Ayako Katagiri's pencil flew over the paper, capturing both their side-by-side pose and that little collar-straightening exchange in barely thirty seconds before she looked up with shining eyes:

"Absolute perfection!! One breezy and bold, the other earnest and attentive—even the arcs of your hems complement each other! I don't need a single shojo manga filter on this panel; the scene is practically sparkling all by itself!"
Looking at the lifelike pair on the page, Ryuji Sakaguchi nodded with a smile:
"True enough—you captured the two of them down to the last detail."
The Observer Who Couldn't Escape Notice
At two-thirty in the afternoon, the doctors' lounge was enjoying a rare quiet spell.

Pushing open the door to pour a glass of water, Ryuji Sakaguchi immediately spotted Ayako Katagiri hunkered down in the farthest armchair, holding an oversized medical journal up as a shield in front of her sketchbook while her eyes darted over the top edge, covertly observing Narumi Jinguji and Sayaka Nanjo chatting over tea by the window.
Catching Sakaguchi's eye, Ayako pressed a finger to her lips and silently mouthed: "Shhh—observing wild doctors in their natural habitat!"
Holding his water cup, Ryuji Sakaguchi raised an eyebrow, before he even had the chance to warn her what tier of master observers she was dealing with—
Standing by the window with her back still turned to the armchair, Narumi Jinguji took a sip of lukewarm black tea and remarked casually in her calm, deadpan alto:
"Ms. Katagiri, if you're sketching the cuff creases on my lab coat—my left sleeve is rolled half a turn higher than the right from washing up after a dressing change, so don't draw them symmetrical."
Ayako Katagiri's pencil froze against the page with a sharp tap:
"Ehhh—?!! Do you have eyes in the back of your head, Dr. Jinguji?!"

Before the echo faded, Sayaka Nanjo—who had been sitting across from Narumi moments earlier—had somehow glided soundlessly behind the armchair, leaning down with a playful, mischievous smile to peek over the corner of Ayako's sketchbook:

"Hehe, Narumi wasn't the only one who noticed, you know. Hiding behind a three-year-old back issue with that bright white nurse cap sticking a whole inch above the cover makes it awfully hard to pretend we don't see you."
Ayako Katagiri scrambled to clap her sketchbook shut:
"Waaah! When did Dr. Nanjo circle around behind me?!"
Blinking gentle yet sly eyes, Sayaka Nanjo steadied the slipping medical journal for her and airily read aloud a tiny margin note in the corner of the page:

"Let's see here... 'Male Doctor Observation Note: Quiet most of the time, yet surprisingly patient whenever coworkers vent about work.' Well, well, Dr. Sakaguchi—looks like our resident manga artist rates you pretty highly, hmm?"
Ryuji Sakaguchi took a resigned sip of water:
"I knew trying stealth reconnaissance on you two could only end one way."
Turning around to look at a thoroughly defeated, beet-red Ayako, Narumi Jinguji let the corner of her mouth curve faintly:
"If you want everyday white-coat material, just pull up a chair and ask—we don't charge modeling fees. That observation note on Sakaguchi, though, is right on the mark."
Pressing both hands to her burning cheeks, Ayako Katagiri let out a plaintive groan:
"Ughhh... Being an observer at Hoshimi Hospital is way too humbling! I feel like I'm the little hamster in a glass tank being observed by the two of you!"

Around nine-ten in the morning, Ryuji Sakaguchi had just crossed the first-floor reception hall when he spotted Asuka Shiromiya pacing slowly in a full circle around Ayako Katagiri, hands clasped behind her back and her expression dead serious.

Subjected to Madam Director's 360-degree inspection, Ayako Katagiri stood stiffly with palms pressed to her skirt seams and chin tucked in, cold sweat practically beading at her temples. The instant she saw Ryuji Sakaguchi passing by, she shot him a desperate SOS look:
"G-Good morning, Dr. Sakaguchi!! I swear I walked through the front doors barely five minutes ago—I haven't set foot near any restricted zone or chatted up a single patient...!"
Stepping closer, Ryuji Sakaguchi caught the gleam in Asuka's eyes—not anger in the slightest, but rather keen aesthetic fascination—and immediately knew what was going on:
"Director Shiromiya, cornering our resident manga artist in the hallway first thing in the morning—have you stumbled onto a new research topic?"
Asuka Shiromiya came to a halt, cupped her chin in one hand, and pointed in earnest at the crown of Ayako's head and the dart line along her waist:

"Be the judge, Dr. Sakaguchi! Coming downstairs just now, it struck me how pairing a high ponytail like Ms. Katagiri's with our hospital's stiff traditional nurse cap gives the brim a fifteen-degree upward tilt in profile that looks wonderfully straight out of a shojo manga! And look at the diagonal tension line along the waist darts when she hugs a thick sketchbook to her chest—"
Frozen in place, Ayako Katagiri blinked:
"...Eh? Y-You're not kicking me out for breaking research rules?"
Asuka Shiromiya looked at her in surprise:

"You've followed the rules impeccably all week—why on earth would I kick you out? I'm seriously debating whether to reference how you wear yours when we revise next season's summer nurse uniform prototypes—refining the cap curvature and reinforcing the heavy-duty pocket seams!"
Ayako Katagiri's shoulders dropped as she exhaled a massive sigh of relief:
"You scared the life out of me... With the way you were staring at me like an inquisitor, Director Shiromiya, I thought my research permit was about to be revoked on the spot!"
Asuka Shiromiya broke into a bright smile, her gaze drifting naturally to the oversized red-lettered acrylic badge on Ayako's left chest as she gave a thoughtful nod:

"And now that it's grown on me, this oversized two-tone bordered badge creates rather a striking pop of color against pure white... What do you think, Dr. Sakaguchi—should we design an enlarged decorative badge for our regular medical staff too?"
Without a moment's hesitation, Ryuji Sakaguchi cast a veto on behalf of the entire hospital staff:

"Let's wrap up the aesthetic exploration right here, Director Shiromiya. If every doctor and nurse in the building leans over a hospital bed wearing a plaque that size, everyone will be knocking their chins on it during auscultation tomorrow morning."
Ayako Katagiri nodded furiously in heartfelt agreement:
"Right, right! Better leave this one-of-a-kind scene-stealing gear as my personal exclusive!"
Honor Student Behind the Fourth-Floor Yellow Line
Where the fourth-floor surgical wing met the public hallway, a bright yellow restricted-access warning line ran crisp and clear across the floor.

Stepping out through the surgical wing's outer airlock door after verifying the next day's instrument packs, Ryuji Sakaguchi and Kaori Miyama immediately spotted Ayako Katagiri standing squarely in the corridor outside—just as Shiori Fujisaki came up from the stairwell carrying an internal-medicine pre-op clearance sheet.
Kaori Miyama halted abruptly, her gaze dropping straight to the tips of Ayako's shoes.

In her spotless white soft-soled nurse shoes, Ayako Katagiri had both toes pressed neatly together, parked down to the millimeter a full two centimeters behind the bright yellow warning line. Straining to make out the perspective of the "SURGERY IN PROGRESS" lightbox inside the doors, she craned her upper body and neck forward as far as they would go while sketching, yet kept her feet rooted to the floor without budging a hair.
Hearing the door click open, Ayako Katagiri looked up at the three of them and proudly pointed the eraser end of her pencil straight down at her toes:

"Dr. Miyama, Dr. Sakaguchi, Shiori! Check out my toes—a full two-centimeter safety margin behind the fourth-floor surgical yellow line! Uniform neat and tidy, shoes properly on, badge front and center!"
Stepping up to glance at the straight yellow stripe, Shiori Fujisaki couldn't help hiding a laugh behind her fingers:
"You're just following basic visitor rules, Ayako—why do you look like you just won gold at nationals?"
Ryuji Sakaguchi chimed in with a smile:
"Making the leap from 'wandering onto an operating table' to 'two-centimeter yellow-line honor student' in the exact same fourth-floor hallway is worth commemorating, at least."

Kaori Miyama glanced from Ayako's shoe tips to her sketchbook, where the perspective lines of the interior ceiling lights looked cramped and slightly warped from trying to peer through frosted glass framing.

After two seconds of silence, Kaori Miyama turned around, grasped the louver dial on the small observation window beside the airlock door, and clicked the slats more than halfway open—revealing a clear, well-lit view of the scrub sinks and the outer corridor by the surgical suites.
Ayako Katagiri's eyes lit up at once:
"Whoa...! Through this little window, the depth perspective is crystal clear!"
Resting one hand on the window frame, Kaori Miyama checked her wristwatch with a calm expression:
"No patient transfers are underway inside right now. You get thirty seconds to block in the structural lines—keep your toes nailed behind that yellow line, and don't step half a millimeter forward."
Ayako Katagiri barked a cheerful "Aye-aye, ma'am!!" and sent her mechanical pencil flying across the page.

Daylight from the hallway windows fell softly over the four of them. Shiori Fujisaki stood quietly smiling at her old classmate sketching away at top speed, while Ryuji Sakaguchi and Kaori Miyama—still holding the louver open as she counted down the seconds—exchanged a glance, an unspoken, easy warmth passing through both their eyes.
Right on the thirty-second mark, Ayako Katagiri lifted her pencil and snapped her sketchbook shut:
